newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer to merge Nevada project.
newsitem.headline: Placer to merge Nevada project.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Tuesday it planned to integrate development of the 2.5 million-ounce gold deposit, South Pipeline, in Nevada, with the adjacent 4.3 million-ounce Pipeline deposit.
Placer Dome said construction of facilities for the combined project was three months ahead of schedule and was expected to be materially under budget.

Facilities to treat ore from the deposits were under construction at the 60 percent-owned Cortez joint venture, with approved expenditure of US$320 million, Placer said. The venture is 40 percent-owned by British-Australian mining conglomerate RTZ-CRA Plc.

It said that by merging South Pipeline, economic returns were being enhanced by the increased throughput of ore. Placer said ore reserves at South Pipeline were estimated to be 44 million tonnes grading 1.75 g/t gold, with total reserves at Pipeline/South Pipeline of 76 million tonnes grading 2.8 g/t gold, containing a total of 6.8 million ounces of gold.
The first gold from Pipeline was expected to be poured in the spring of 1997, Placer said.

Ore from both deposits will be treated in the new carbon-in-leach (CIL) gold recovery plant now under construction, which has increased capacity to a nominal 7,250 tonnes per day from 4,200 tonnes a day.

Placer said total combined gold production was expected to average 440,000 ounces of gold a year over a 12-year mine life, up from 310,000 ounces per year for Pipeline alone, at a cash production cost of US$152 per ounce.
